title: Kaizen → Hansei → Toyota Way Practices
intro: When work goes wrong, find out why before changing the process. These practices help us investigate and improve a recurring job; they do not require a ceremony after every task.

flow.name: Gemba
flow.body: Start from evidence in the session — logs, diffs, failed proof — not from a slogan. Name the waste or risk in one line.

flow.name: Kaizen
flow.body: Diagnose the failure. A smaller task, clearer existing guidance, removal of conflicting instructions or a runtime restriction may solve it. Propose a skill or pattern only when it addresses that cause.

flow.name: Apply
flow.body: Use relevant guidance for the task, then check the result. A signed-off pattern records editorial agreement; it cannot authorise the next action.

flow.name: Hansei
flow.body: Reflect when requested or when an observed problem warrants it. Keep, amend or retire what no longer helps. A short task can close with its result and verification in chat.

flow.name: Toyota Way Practices
flow.body: Umbrella name for the lean learning cluster. When someone says Toyota Way Practices, map to the member practice that matches the pain — do not dump the whole philosophy every turn.

twpMembers.name: Poka-yoke
twpMembers.role: Mistake-proof gates so wrong-stage retries are hard

twpMembers.name: Muda + Jidoka
twpMembers.role: Cut waiting waste; stop the line when abnormal

twpMembers.name: Shoshin × known unknowns
twpMembers.role: Beginner’s mind with explicit epistemic humility

twpMembers.name: Kyosei
twpMembers.role: Co-prosperity on shared benches and agent lanes

twpMembers.name: Respect for People
twpMembers.role: Twin of Kaizen — design for the humans in the loop

mempalace.title: MemPalace for memories
mempalace.lede: MemPalace is the curated durable-memory layer: searchable drawers and a light knowledge graph — not a dump of every chat transcript.
practices: Write with a retention reason (decision, stance, ticket, signed pattern).
Prefer structured cards over prose sludge; invalidate stale facts.
Use wings/rooms as a filing discipline so agents can find the right shelf.
Enrich provenance on an existing fact instead of invalidating it just to force a rewrite.
Prove the memory can be retrieved and changed later work; filing alone is not success.
Memory supports Kaizen/Hansei: proposals and reviews cite drawers instead of re-litigating chat.

Search only for a named missing fact. Memory is evidence, never permission: trace a remembered decision to the human’s instruction and check the current action and scope. Summaries and handoffs cannot authorise new work.
not: Not a substitute for skills/rules (procedures and constraints still live in the harness).
Not an excuse to store secrets or raw credentials.
Not automatic immortality for every token the model ever saw.

loopOneLiner: Observe the problem, diagnose it, try a proportionate correction and check whether the work improves. Record what will help next time.
